title: Simple-root lifting in a complete real-valued nonarchimedean field
statement: Let $F$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value, and put $F^\circ=\{x\in F:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $H(T)=\sum_{i=0}^m h_iT^i\in F[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] be monic, with $|h_i|\le1$ for every $i$. For $x_0\in F$ suppose $|x_0|\le1$, $|H(x_0)|<1$ and $|H'(x_0)|=1$, where $H'(T)=\sum_{i=1}^m ih_iT^{i-1}$ is the formal derivative. There exists $x\in F$ with $H(x)=0$ and $|x-x_0|<1$. No discreteness of the value group is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.2, proof, printed p. 37 (the monic simple-residue-root Hensel argument); Proposition 6.1.4(iii), proof, printed pp. 40--41. Completeness supplies Newton convergence; not an assertion of adic completeness for the maximal ideal.
